items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: See, Jimmy played with Buddy Bowling and those guys.

ctx.x: Well, I imagine he was busy with his band.

Always busy. Always busy. And I had one of the musicians in my band as a product of those old bands, one of my first bands, that was old Jimmy Johnson. See, Jimmy played with Buddy Bowling and those guys.
Did he read much or was he fake?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: with what's the trumpet player, the first one? Buddy Bowling.

ctx.x: Did you ever see him on a bicycle? Somebody was telling me he used to even ride a bicycle.

Well, if it was, it was in the days that he was playing here with Bunk Jones, not with Bunk, with what's the trumpet player, the first one? Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling. Maybe in those days he might have been a younger man. He might have rode a bicycle then. You mean with that bass on his back? Yeah. Yes, I've heard him say that. I mentioned Larry Cottrell's daddy yesterday at the concert. I used to lug those drums all the way from his house up to Clay Hall Street. And then there was a whole set of drums on his…
Well, he had special drums, too, though, they said.

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: He's got a nice write up in a new book on Buddy Balbrin.

ctx.x: No, we got the bass player about a couple of three months after that.
And who was he? The Jimmy Johnson. He's got a nice write up in a new book on Buddy Balbrin.
Well, he was a great man, a great bass player. Oh, yeah.
